title.value: Architecture of Normal Faults in Shallow-Water Carbonates of Central Italy: Preliminary Data

note.value:
Preliminary data on the structural arrangement of fractures and fault rocks along four, basin bounding, normal faults are here presented. These are active faults crosscutting Mesozoic-Cenozoic, shallow-water carbonates of central Italy, which controlled the formation of late Pliocene-Quaternary small, elongated continental basins during regional uplift. Field data are consistent with a systematic arrangement of fault rocks and structures in the faults. In the footwalls, cm- to m-thick zones of cemented, clast/matrix -supported cataclasite, and gouge are present close to the adjacent the faults. Further away, there are decameter(s) wide less- damaged carbonates. The Quaternary rock on the hanging walls is mainly composed of fluvial- lacustrine sediments and alluvium, which are often brecciated in the vicinity of the faults. At depth, faulting started with diffuse carbonates brecciation, enhanced fluid flow, and consequent cementation/veining. During exhumation, slip clustered into the fault cores, and successively localized at the current hanging wall-footwall contacts once the Quaternary sediments were juxtaposed against carbonates.

Low-Mg calcite formed around the fault planes due to the infiltration of a meteoric fluid. Minerals precipitated in the spaces among the individual survivor clasts, and in the net of fractures, binding the clasts together. The fault rock geochemistry is consistent with fluid infiltration into the faults either at the land surface and/or after having moved through the hanging wall sediments. Currently, three of the four faults form combined Conduit-Barrier permeability structure to fluid flow, in which relative impermeables of gouge/cataclasites separate the wide damage zones that formed in the footwalls from the fault planes. The 2D values of porosity of samples from these rocks are between 6.4 and 11.1%. The Monte Capo di Serre fault, which has a peculiar architecture, behaves as a local conduit to fluid flow.
Agosta, Fabrizio. (2002). Architecture of Normal Faults in Shallow-Water Carbonates of Central Italy: Preliminary Data. Stanford Digital Repository. Available at: http://purl.stanford.edu/cr195nx8428
